title_en: Interpretation of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Article 104 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: I. The 'uphold the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, and bear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China' as prescribed in Article 104 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China shall be both the legal content that must be included in the oath as prescribed in that Article, and the legal requirements and conditions for standing for election or assuming the public offices listed in that Article.

II. The provision in Article 104 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China that relevant public officers 'must, in accordance with law, take an oath when assuming office' has the following implications:
(1) Taking the oath is a legal condition and a mandatory procedure for the assumption of office by the public officers listed in that Article. Those who have not taken a lawful and valid oath or who have refused to take the oath shall not assume the corresponding public office and shall not exercise the corresponding powers or enjoy the corresponding benefits.
(2) The oath must comply with the legal requirements as to form and content. The oath-taker must take the oath sincerely and solemnly, and must accurately, completely, and solemnly read the legal oath which includes the content of 'uphold the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China, and bear allegiance to the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China'.
(3) If the oath-taker refuses to take the oath, he or she shall lose the eligibility to assume the corresponding public office as listed in that Article. If the oath-taker intentionally reads an oath that is inconsistent with the legal oath or takes the oath in any insincere or unsolemn manner, it shall also be considered as refusal to take the oath, and the oath taken shall be invalid, and the oath-taker shall lose the eligibility to assume the corresponding public office as listed in that Article.
(4) The oath must be taken before the person authorized to administer the oath as prescribed by law. The person administering the oath shall be responsible for ensuring that the oath-taking is conducted lawfully. The oath shall be determined as valid if it complies with this Interpretation and the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; the oath shall be determined as invalid if it does not comply with this Interpretation and the laws of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and no re-taking of the oath shall be arranged.

III. The oath prescribed in Article 104 of the Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China is a legal commitment made by the public officers listed in that Article to the People's Republic of China and its Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and has legal binding force. The oath-taker must truly believe in and strictly abide by the legal oath. An oath-taker who makes a false oath or engages in conduct that violates the oath after taking the oath shall bear legal liability according to law.
The above is hereby announced.
